name: Remdesivir
drug_class: Nucleotide analogue RNA polymerase inhibitor (adenosine analogue prodrug)
route_note: IV infusion once daily; 3-day course in non-hospitalised high-risk patients, 5–10 days in hospital

discovery.note: Emerged from Gilead's programme of 1'-cyano C-nucleoside analogues against RNA viruses (hepatitis C, RSV); broad activity against Ebola and coronaviruses was later found.

tagline: The first antiviral fully approved for COVID-19, given by infusion
summary: Remdesivir is an intravenous phosphoramidate prodrug of an adenosine nucleotide analogue that inhibits viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Tested first against Ebola, it became the first drug approved by the FDA for COVID-19 in October 2020. It shortens recovery in hospitalised patients and reduces hospitalisation when given early to high-risk outpatients.
mechanism: Remdesivir enters cells and is converted to its active triphosphate form (GS-443902), which competes with ATP for incorporation by the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.

Once incorporated, it causes delayed chain termination: the polymerase adds a few more nucleotides and then stalls, because the 1'-cyano group clashes with the enzyme. Its relative resistance to the coronavirus proofreading exonuclease contributes to its activity.
uses: COVID-19 in hospitalised adults and children
COVID-19 in non-hospitalised patients at high risk of progression (3-day course)

history.title: Ebola activity
history.detail: Gilead and US Army researchers report that GS-5734 protects rhesus monkeys from Ebola virus.

history.title: PALM trial
history.detail: In the Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola trial, remdesivir is less effective than the antibody treatments and that arm is stopped.

history.title: Emergency use
history.detail: After the ACTT-1 trial shows faster recovery, the FDA issues an emergency use authorisation on 1 May 2020; Japan and the EU (conditional) approve it soon after.

history.title: WHO Solidarity
history.detail: Interim results of the WHO Solidarity trial show little or no effect on mortality, and WHO briefly advises against routine use.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Veklury becomes the first FDA-approved COVID-19 treatment on 22 October 2020.

history.title: Outpatients
history.detail: Based on the PINETREE trial, the FDA extends approval to a 3-day course for high-risk non-hospitalised patients.

pk.half_life: remdesivir about 1 h; nucleoside metabolite GS-441524 about 27 h
pk.metabolism: hydrolases (carboxylesterase 1, cathepsin A) and phosphorylation to the active triphosphate

facts: Remdesivir was originally investigated for hepatitis C and respiratory syncytial virus before being tested against Ebola.
Its sulfobutylether-beta-cyclodextrin excipient was a reason for initial caution in severe kidney disease; the US label no longer requires dose adjustment.

references.title: Beigel JH et al. Remdesivir for the treatment of Covid-19 — final report. NEJM 2020
